findings.reason: a builder implementing "writes a renewal time into its own registration" literally reuses the in-place writer and ships a mechanism that intermittently reads a fresh registration as gone, so §8 must state how the renewal survives a concurrent cross-host read (an atomic sibling write, or a reader that retries a record it could not parse) and how often it is written.
findings.text: §8 has the follower write its lease renewal "into its own registration", but that file is rewritten in place (`_write_watch_record`, reckon/crew/run_paths.py:50-57, truncates then writes, no rename) and it is read by the producer on another host, which by §8's own premise cannot take the lock to serialise against the writer — so a read landing between truncate and write yields `record == {}`, the renewal reads missing, and a healthy foreign follower is judged gone, reproducing exactly the "no producer" symptom §8 exists to remove; the plan bounds neither the write cadence nor the read's tolerance of a torn record

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — each cited symbol resolves at base: `producer_lease_seconds` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1702), `renew_producer_lease` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1764), `_follower_liveness` (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:482), `watch_state` and `seat_names_a_live_foreign_producer` (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:161, :143), `session_follower_released` (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:205, reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:708), `freshness` (reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:369), `not_fresh_line` (reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:729), and both landed test files exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §8's and §9's done-whens are measurable in a temporary crew home and each declares a negative control that fails the pre-fix code (`foreign judged by its lock again` reads the fresh-renewal case gone; `freshness` returning `no-producer` again fails §9's first case), and both carry suite-delta clauses naming the exceptions.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections log their negative control under the run directory and cite the durable archive record `docs/evidence/archive/a-seat-held-elsewhere-is-not-restarted-landed.html`; §8's post-merge confirmation names `~/.config/reckon/crew/obligations/reckon/`, a durable path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the new symbols or test filenames (`test_a_follower_on_another_node_renews_a_lease.py`, `test_a_missing_snapshot_names_a_live_seat.py`), and the prose states mechanisms rather than tracker entries.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's stated root cause (node-local `flock` makes a foreign registration read gone; §4 judged it by that lock) matches the cited evidence and the code path, but the repair's mechanism does not reliably produce its own done-when, because it writes the renewal into a file that the judging host reads without the lock that would serialise the read.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 names one deliverable (a foreign follower registration judged by a renewed lease) and §9 names one (the hook line for a missing snapshot beside a live foreign seat); the test rewrites in each are consequences of that deliverable, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9's dependency on §8 is carried by gate `g-sheinr-1` (`data-section="s9"`, `data-gated-sections="s9"`, required-evidence `#s8`) and by followup f-sheinr-003, and §8's write paths (`reckon/crew/follower_registration.py`, `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`) do not overlap §9's, so the declared parallel/gated split is correct.
